text: A psalm of David. I will sing of mercy and justice; to you, LORD, I will make music.
I will give heed to the way of integrity — when will you come to me? I will walk with a blameless heart within my house.
I will set no vile thing before my eyes. I hate the deeds of those who turn aside; they will not cling to me.

versions.text: I will set no worthless thing before my eyes. I hate the work of those who fall away; it will not cling to me.
versions.explanation: דְּבַר־בְּלִיָּעַל is stronger than 'worthless thing' — it denotes something base or vile. 'Those who fall away' is ambiguous; סֵטִים means those who turn aside (from the right way). Also 'it will not cling to me' has an unclear antecedent; plural 'they' matches 'deeds' more naturally in oral reading.

text: The crooked of heart shall depart from me; I will know nothing of evil.

versions.text: A crooked heart shall be far from me; I will have nothing to do with evil.
versions.explanation: יָסוּר means 'shall depart/turn away from me' rather than the static 'be far from me'; and לֹא אֵדָע is literally 'I will not know,' which the rendering 'I will know nothing of evil' preserves while still reading naturally.

text: Whoever slanders his neighbor in secret, him I will destroy. The one with haughty eyes and a proud heart I will not endure.

versions.text: Whoever slanders his neighbor in secret, him I will silence. The one with haughty eyes and an arrogant heart I will not endure.
versions.explanation: אַצְמִית means 'destroy, put an end to,' which is stronger than 'silence'; 'silence' also obscures the parallel with verse 8 where the same verb is paired with 'cutting off.' Consider keeping 'destroy' in both places for consistency.

text: My eyes are on the faithful of the land, that they may dwell with me. The one who walks in the way of integrity shall serve me.
No one who practices deceit shall live in my house; no one who speaks lies shall stand before my eyes.
Morning by morning I will silence all the wicked of the land, cutting off every evildoer from the city of the LORD.
